item.title: Travel Rules and Work Rights Shift
item.description: Travel rules, work rights and everyday services shift in several practical ways.
item.content:encoded:
Travel rules, work rights and everyday services shift in several practical ways.

  1. Thailand halves NZ visa-free stays from 15 September Thailand’s revised visa-exemption rules take effect on 15 September: New Zealand ordinary-passport holders remain visa-exempt for tourism, but the initial stay falls from 60 days to 30 days; travellers who enter by 14 September keep the stay granted under the old rules. 4 Sep 2026. Thai Government · Royal Thai Embassy · Follow up
  2. New Zealand passes nationwide small-boat lifejacket rule Parliament has passed legislation requiring people on recreational craft 6 metres or shorter to wear a correctly fitted lifejacket whenever the vessel is underway; the skipper is responsible, with exemptions including surfers, sports events and stand-up-paddleboard surfing. 4 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  3. Australian credit-card travel insurance is being cut back CommBank will remove all included insurance from several card tiers and reduce benefits on others from 29 September, while Westpac is changing its complimentary credit-card insurance policy from 1 October; travellers relying on Australian cards should re-check cover before booking. 4 Sep 2026. CommBank · Westpac · Follow up
  4. Australia’s EV sales overtake petrol for the first time Battery-electric vehicles reached about 27,000 sales and 24.9% of Australia’s new-car market in August, exceeding petrol-car sales of about 25,800 and diesel sales of about 23,600 for the first time. 4 Sep 2026. FCAI data report · Follow up
  5. GPT-6 Astra begins rollout OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on 3 September, initially to a limited set of organisations, with broader access for paid ChatGPT plans and the API due over the following days; the model adds stronger coding, research, computer-use and multi-step work capabilities. 3 Sep 2026. OpenAI · Follow up
  6. Google deploys WeatherNext 3 across consumer products Google launched WeatherNext 3 with hourly global forecast updates, real-time satellite inputs and substantially higher spatial resolution, and began integrating its forecasts into Search, Gemini, Maps and Google Maps Platform. 3 Sep 2026. Google · TechCrunch · Follow up
  7. Google adds conversational voice control to Gmail, Docs and Keep Google began rolling out Gemini 3.5 Live voice features that can search Gmail, draft in Docs and turn spoken thoughts into organised Keep notes for eligible Workspace and business subscribers. 3 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  8. New Zealand’s replacement leave law is now enacted The Employment Leave Act 2026 has received Royal assent and will replace the Holidays Act on 6 August 2028, changing how annual, sick, bereavement, family-violence and alternative leave are earned, taken and paid; current Holidays Act rules remain in force until then. 7 Aug 2026. Employment New Zealand · NZ Legislation · Follow up
  9. Two New Zealand psychiatrists can now prescribe MDMA for PTSD Medsafe has authorised two psychiatrists to prescribe pharmaceutical-grade MDMA to selected PTSD patients in supervised clinical treatment plans; MDMA remains an unapproved medicine and patients will not receive it to take home. 4 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  10. SH58’s new Moonshine Road roundabout fully opens The new Moonshine Road roundabout on State Highway 58 is now open in both directions after westbound traffic began using it this week; a temporary 30 km/h limit remains while project work continues. 4 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  11. SH2 through Carterton reopens both ways for the weekend The rebuilt southbound lane near Andersons Line is complete and State Highway 2 through Carterton is reopening in both directions on Friday evening; the remaining northbound rebuild has been postponed after unexpected soft ground was found. 4 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  12. West Coast highway weather disruption persists State Highway 7 is down to one lane near Heslop Creek Bridge after fallen trees, while State Highway 73 from Arthur’s Pass Village to Kumara Junction has an area warning for slips and flooding, affecting South Island cross-island road travel. 4 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  13. JB Hi-Fi opens a new central Wellington store JB Hi-Fi’s new store at 29A Brandon Street opens with a public launch on 5 September, adding another large electronics retailer in central Wellington; the opening includes a four-hour in-store Cost + GST promotion and a free street event. 3–5 Sep 2026. WellyBuzz · Follow up
  14. Interislander unions give notice of partial action Interislander union members have notified partial industrial action for 18 September: affected members will refuse to load KiwiRail cargo units and decline callbacks and overtime for the day, while ferry sailings themselves are not scheduled to stop. 4 Sep 2026. B2BNews · Follow up
  15. New Zealand proposes compulsory asbestos testing for sand products The Government has proposed an unsafe-goods notice requiring pre-sale asbestos testing for toys containing sand and decorative, art and craft products containing sand, after 23 recalls covering about 46,000 products. 4 Sep 2026. Beehive · Follow up
  16. Global food-price index reaches its highest since 2022 The FAO Food Price Index rose to 133.3 points in August from a revised 130.8 in July, its highest level since late 2022, with all major commodity categories increasing over the month. 4 Sep 2026. FAO report · Ajel · Follow up
  17. KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal change reaches Parliament The Government has introduced the KiwiSaver (First Home or Farm) Amendment Bill, which would let workers in service tenancies such as farm workers use KiwiSaver first-home withdrawals without having to move out of employer-provided accommodation, and also changes first-farm purchase rules. 2 Sep 2026. NZ Government · Follow up
  18. New trans-Tasman programme targets business barriers New Zealand and Australia launched a business-government programme to reduce cross-Tasman operating costs and reported a 30% increase in joint trans-Tasman standards, with work spanning regulatory coherence, supply chains, technology and other shared areas. 4 Sep 2026. NZ Government · Follow up
